Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:10:1.english: Astrology - One who gazes at the stars.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:10:2.english: They would rise early to his door - To take counsel from him.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:10:3.hebrew: אידלי יומא - הוגבה שמש, כשהחמה זורחת:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:10:3.english: The day was raised [lit., "lifted"] - The sun was lifted up, when the sun shines.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:10:4.english: The harvest has lightened - It eases the illness.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:12:1.hebrew: עדשין אין להן פה - כמו שיש לפולין ולשאר מיני קטנית כמין סדק:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:12:1.english: Lentils have no mouth - Like what broad beans and other kinds of legumes have, a kind of crack.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:12:2.hebrew: אבל אין לו פה - שהוא יושב ודומם:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:12:2.english: But it has no mouth - For it sits and is silent.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:12:3.hebrew: לנחומי בביעי - אין להם פה, אבל אינם מגלגלים כגלגל:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:12:3.english: To comfort [mourners] with eggs - They have no mouth, but they do not roll like a wheel.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:13:1.hebrew: ושט את הבכורה - וביזה את העבודה שהיתה בבכורות. שט תרגום של בזיון: ״מדוע הקילתני״ (שמואל ב י״ט:מ״ד), תרגום יונתן: ״אשטתני״:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:13:1.english: And he despised the birthright - And he scorned the [Temple] service that was performed by the firstborn. [The word] "shat" is the Aramaic translation of contempt: "Why did you treat me with contempt?" (II Samuel 19:44); Targum Yonatan [renders it]: "ashtatani."

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:2:3.english: And she becomes slack - [It is] an expression of looseness.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:3:1.hebrew: שאין אדם נתפס - להתחייב על שהוא מדבר קשה מחמת צער ויסורין. דקאמר "לא בדעת ידבר", לא אמר "לא ברשע ידבר", אלא "לא בדעת":
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:3:1.english: That a person is not held [accountable] - to be held liable for speaking harshly because of pain and suffering. For it says, "He does not speak with knowledge"; it did not say, "He does not speak wickedly," but rather, "not with knowledge."

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:5:1.hebrew: כלילי הוו להו - כתרים, ובכל כתר שלשה פרצופים, ואיש את שמו מחוקק על פרצופו. וכשבאין יסורין על אחד מהן, פרצופו משתנה. וכן אילני:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:5:1.english: They had crowns - Crowns, and in each crown [were] three faces, and each man's name was engraved on his face. And when suffering came upon one of them, his face would change. And likewise [with] the trees.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:5:2.english: [When the trees] withered - [In Old French:] fletrie (withered).

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:5:3.hebrew: או חברא כחברי דאיוב - אם אין לו לאדם אוהבים, נוח לו שימות:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:5:3.english: Or a friend like the friends of Job - If a person has no friends, it is better for him to die.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:6:1.english: "To multiply upon the face of the earth, and daughters were born," etc.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:6:2.hebrew: רביה באה לעולם - כשנולדה בת, לפי שממהרת להיות לו זרע:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:6:2.english: Increase came into the world - When a daughter was born, because she hastens to produce offspring for him.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:7:1.hebrew: הוכפלו ביופי - ואין לך כפל טוב ממנו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:7:1.english: They were doubled in beauty - And there is no doubling better than it.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:8:1.english: That she resembled the day - Bright like the sun.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:8:2.english: Like Ketzia - It is a type of perfume.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:8:3.hebrew: קרנא דקרש - מין חיה, וקרניה משחירין כמו צבע:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:8:3.english: The horn of the karash - [The karash is] a kind of animal, and its horns turn black like a dye.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:8:4.hebrew: כורכמא דרישקא - כרכום של גן, הגדל בגינה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:8:4.english: Saffron of the garden bed (rishka) - Garden saffron, which grows in a garden.

Rashi on Bava Batra 16b:8:5.english: In its kind - For it is superior to the other kinds of spices.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 16b:10:1.hebrew: שכל חולה שרואה אותה מיד מתרפא - וא"ת: והא בימי אברהם אכתי לא היה חולי בעולם, כדאמרי' בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ דף פז.), דעד יעקב לא הוה חולשא, ועד אלישע לא הוה דאיחלש ואיתפח! ומצינן למימר דהכא בחולה של מכה איירי. ור"ת ור"י מפרשים דעד יעקב לא הוה דאיחלש היינו חולי של מיתה; מכאן ואילך הוה דאיחלש חולי של מיתה, ולא הוה דאיתפח עד אלישע:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 16b:10:1.english: That every sick person who sees it is immediately healed - And if you ask: But in the days of Abraham there was not yet illness in the world, as we say in [the chapter] "HaSokher et HaPoalim" (Bava Metzia 87a), that until Jacob there was no weakness [before death], and until Elisha there was no one who fell ill and recovered! One can answer that here [the Gemara] is speaking of a person ill from a wound. And Rabbeinu Tam and Rabbi Yitzchak explain that "until Jacob there was no one who fell ill" refers to a fatal illness; from then on there was [someone] who fell ill with a fatal illness, and there was no one who recovered [from it] until Elisha:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 16b:13:1.hebrew: בא על נערה המאורסה - ואם תאמר: והלא לא נצטוו בני נח על נערה המאורסה, כדאמרינן בפרק ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין דף נז: ושם ד"ה לנערה): בעולת בעל יש להן, נכנסת לחופה ולא נבעלה אין להן. ואומר רבינו יצחק, דאף על פי שלא נצטוו, מכל מקום מכוער הדבר, כמו "ושט את הבכורה" אף על פי שאינו מצווה על כך:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 16b:13:1.english: He had relations with a betrothed young woman - And if you say: But were the descendants of Noah not commanded regarding a betrothed young woman? As we say in the chapter "Arba Mitot" (Sanhedrin 57b, and there, s.v. "lena'arah"): [The prohibition applies to] a woman who was married and had relations with her husband (be'ulat ba'al); [but] one who entered the wedding canopy and was not yet intimately with her husband, they have none. And Rabbi Yitzchak says that even though they were not commanded [about this], in any case the matter is disgraceful, like [Esau's sin of] "and he despised the birthright," even though he was not commanded about it.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 16b:18:1.hebrew: שלשה כו' מעין העולם הבא - תימה לרשב"א: אמאי לא חשיב נמי איוב, דאמר לעיל (בבא בתרא דף טו:): "והאתונות רועות על ידיהם" — מלמד שהטעימו הקב"ה מעין עולם הבא? וי"ל דאיוב לא היה אלא בחד מילתא, ואברהם ויצחק ויעקב נהנו מעין עוה"ב מכל וכל:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 16b:18:1.english: "Three...a semblance of the World to Come" - The Rashba found it puzzling: Why doesn't [the Gemara] also count Iyov, as it said above (Bava Batra 15b): "'And the she-donkeys were grazing beside them'—this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave them a taste of a semblance of the World to Come"? And one can answer that Iyov [experienced this] only in one matter, whereas Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov enjoyed a semblance of the World to Come in every respect.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 16b:8:1.hebrew: ככוחלא דרישקא במינה - אע"ג דכחול הוא שחור, כדפירש בה"ג "אוכמא אוכמא" [חולין מו:] — היינו דמיא לכוחלא. ה"פ: כי היכי דכוחלא דרישקא מקרין ומאיר משאר כוחלא, כך היא היתה נאה משאר נשים; וקרן הפוך — לשון "כי קרן עור פני משה" (שמות ל״ד:ל״ה). והשתא אתי שפיר הא דמייתי "ותקרעי בפוך עיניך", דכחול דומה לפוך, שנותנין כחול בעין. אבל לפירוש רש"י דגרס "כי כורכמא דרישקא", קשה לרשב"א: א"כ מאי מייתי "ותקרעי בפוך עיניך"? ויונתן תרגם "נרד וכרכום" — "רשק וכרכום; כפרים עם נרדים עם רישקא" (שיר השירים ד׳:י״ג):
Tosafot on Bava Batra 16b:8:1.english: Like the kohl of Rishka, in its kind - Although kohl is black, as Behag explained: "ukhma, ukhma" [Chullin 46b], this means she was similar to kohl. Its meaning is: Just as the kohl of Rishka shines and gives light more than other kohl, so she was more beautiful than other women; and [the name] Keren Hapukh is an expression of "for the skin of Moses' face shone [karan]" (Exodus 34:35). And now it is well understood why [the Gemara] brings "and you tear your eyes with puakh," since kohl is similar to puakh, for they apply kohl to the eye. But according to Rashi's explanation, who reads "like saffron of Rishka," it is difficult, according to the Rashba: If so, why does [the Gemara] bring "and you tear your eyes with puakh"? And Yonatan translated "nard and saffron" as "rashak and saffron"; "henna with nards" [as] "with rishka" (Song of Songs 4:13).
